standard.title: Indian Standard Identification Colours for Schemes for Ships' Ventilation Systems
standard.description: This standard specifies the identification colours for functional plans of ventilation systems on board ships. It is intended to be applied only when identification of such systems by color is deemed necessary to ensure clear communication and structural safety.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the identification colours for functional plans of ventilation systems on board ships. It is intended to be applied only when identification of such systems by color is deemed necessary to ensure clear communication and structural safety.

certification.description: Voluntary Engineering Practice and Drafting Standard. Since IS 9423:1980 is a procedural code of practice for design office schematics rather than a safety-critical consumer product, it is certified on a voluntary basis. However, compliance with this standard is universally mandated inside all Indian Navy, Coast Guard, public shipyards (e.g., MDL, GRSE, GSL), commercial shipbuilders, and maritime classification societies (such as IRS and Lloyd's Register) during the approval of functional ventilation, HVAC, and outfitting drawings.
requirements: Specifies identification colours for functional plans to be used for ventilation systems on board ships, only when identification by colour is necessary to ensure safety and system clarity.
Explicitly notes that the colour references given in Table 1 are for guidance only, allowing minor variations in paint shades as long as system distinctions remain unambiguous.
